title: Data sojourn policy for interactive artifacts with legal-handoff packaging
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Scope: implement a configurable 'sojourn' policy that controls how long user prompts, model responses, request logs, and derived metrics remain addressable in the primary data store before automated packaging, compaction, or deletion. Deliver a machine-readable export format (forensic bundle) that satisfies legal/incident requests and automated evidence pipelines. Goals: (1) Console and API hooks to configure per-tenant and per-route sojourn durations and sampling rules; (2) background worker that compacts/transforms data into evidence bundles, performs integrity hashing and optional customer KMS encryption for offsite archival; (3) automated manifest and telemetry so that exports are auditable and replayable for QA/legal. Out of scope: full UI for policy inheritance visualization (follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Console and API endpoints allow setting sojourn durations per route and per tenant (min granularity: 1 hour)
Background packager produces a signed forensic bundle (.tar.gz + manifest.json) containing: sampled prompts/responses, request logs, metric summaries, and a SHA256 index for each artifact
"Bundle lifecycle" documented: proof of deletion from hot store, archival location, and evidence retention metadata
Automated export supports customer-managed KMS wrapping for bundles and produces export S3 URL with time-limited signed access
Audit trail entries generated for every policy change, export, and deletion, and surfaceable via Console and API
Performance: packaging worker maintains <10% additional CPU overhead on ingestion pipeline under normal traffic for a 1M req/day tenant (measured in staging)
design_decisions: Use term 'sojourn' to differentiate policy intent (short-term operational accessibility) from long-term retention/archival
Two-tier packaging: immediate compact (prefix + KV cache snapshot) for fast forensic triage, and deep archival bundle for legal export
Sampling rules are expressed as 'deterministic reservoir sampling' seeded by tenant-id to allow reproducible bundles for repeated exports
Evidence manifest is JSONL with flat metadata fields only (no nested objects) to simplify downstream parsing for legal teams
Integrate with existing audit log pipeline and reuse trace IDs to link packaging jobs to original requests
implementation_notes: Add retention_policy table: columns (tenant_id, route_id, sojourn_seconds, sampling_rate, sample_mode, last_modified_by, last_modified_at)

New background service 'sojourn-packager' subscribes to compacted Kafka topic, applies sampling, constructs artifacts, computes SHA256 for each file, signs manifest with platform signing key, optionally uploads to customer KMS-wrapped S3 bucket
Provide 'export-v2' API: POST /v2/exports with params {tenant, route, start_ts, end_ts, purpose, kms_key_id?}. Returns job id and progress endpoints
Console UX: per-route dropdown with presets (Operational: 7d, Compliance: 90d, Minimal: 24h) and advanced mode for ISO timestamps and sampling controls
Ensure cold-storage records keep only hashed references and provenance metadata; raw text removed once boxed into signed bundle and archivable
Retention enforcement will run as scheduled jobs that first create a proof-of-packaging snapshot before deleting hot artifacts
Metrics: expose packager job duration, bytes packaged, and bundle verification success rate to runtime-telemetry
tradeoffs_and_risks: Keeping per-route short sojourn increases operational cost (storage + packaging), mitigated via sampling and compacted artifacts
Customer-managed KMS increases integration complexity and failure modes — provide fallback auto-keying and clear error semantics
Deterministic sampling aids reproducibility but may under-represent low-frequency PII patterns; require targeted always-capture flags for flagged investigations
Signing with platform key simplifies verification for platform operators but customers requiring independent attestation will need HSM-wrapped keys (future work)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement API + packager; run on internal test tenants and two pilot customers; collect metrics and storage cost impact (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta): expose Console controls to selected customers, add KMS integration, and validate bundle ingestion for legal teams (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (ga): enable self-serve in Console with default presets and full audit trail; update docs and incident playbook (2 weeks)
Rollback: if packager causes >5% error rate or exceeds CPU budget, disable packaging for non-critical tenants and revert to silent archival mode
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampling determinism and manifest generation
Integration tests for KMS wrap/unwrap flows using test keys
Load test simulating 1M/day tenant to measure packager resource usage
E2E validation: create export, verify bundle contains required artifacts and SHA256 matches uploaded files
Security review and pen-test focused on export endpoints and signed manifest verification
notes: Initial design collaborators: Maya Chen (Product), Leo Grant (Security), Priya Nair (Console UX)
Related legal requirement reference: EU eDiscovery guidance & state-specific data sovereignty constraints
